acceptance_criteria: AC-1 (real bug, found live during AC-5 demonstration 1, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012 seq 3-4): scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py's pre-push privacy-gate hook (GOV_PO_3 section 3.4 item 1) currently runs scan_repository() against the FULL working tree and fails closed on ANY finding, including findings already present on origin/main before the current movement's changes -- confirmed live: two pre-existing prose false positives (project/build_history.json:47, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003-...json:155, both build-history-immutable, never to be edited to silence the scanner) blocked an entirely unrelated one-file movement's push. This blocks every future orchestrated movement's push for as long as any pre-existing finding remains anywhere in the repository, which defeats the hook's own purpose (catching NEW leaks this movement introduces) and silently removes the human-judgment override that has, until now, let engineers manually confirm 'pre-existing, unrelated' and proceed (documented repeatedly this session, e.g. PR #124's own CI precedent).

AC-2: the hook becomes baseline-aware: before push, it runs scan_repository() twice -- once against the current working tree (post-changes), once against the movement's own recorded base commit (report.git.base from the relay SESSION_START, already resolved to base_sha in the orchestrator's process record, §3.5/§3.7 of GOV_PO_3) checked out to a throwaway location or via git show at that ref for each flagged file. A finding present in BOTH scans (same file, same line-region, same finding type) is pre-existing debt -- do not block. A finding present ONLY in the post-changes scan is genuinely new -- block, exactly as today.

AC-3: the baseline diff must be robust to line-number drift (a pre-existing finding whose line number shifted because of unrelated earlier lines in the same file, without the flagged content itself changing, must still count as pre-existing, not new) -- match on (file, finding_type, a stable content fingerprint of the flagged span) rather than (file, exact line number) alone.

AC-4: the hook's denial message, when it does block, names exactly which finding(s) are new (only those, not the pre-existing ones alongside them) so the engineer session gets an actionable, minimal report.

AC-5: performance is bounded -- the baseline scan runs once per push attempt (not once per file), and is skipped entirely (no baseline comparison overhead) on the common case where the post-changes scan already reports zero findings.

AC-6: targeted tests: a synthetic repo-shape fixture with (a) a pre-existing finding untouched by the diff -- push allowed; (b) a pre-existing finding whose containing file the diff also touches elsewhere -- still allowed if the flagged span itself is unchanged; (c) a genuinely new finding -- push denied, message names only the new one; (d) a pre-existing finding whose line number shifted due to unrelated earlier edits in the same file -- still recognized as pre-existing (AC-3). Also a regression test reproducing the exact live bug (the two real findings named in AC-1, run against this repository's real current state) proving the fix resolves this movement's own motivating incident.

AC-7: validation and state: targeted tests green; tests/test_orchestrator.py unaffected (this hook lives in nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py, not orchestrator.py itself); project-state bookkeeping in this PR.

entries.text: Implemented AC-1..AC-7: scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py's pre-push privacy gate is now baseline-aware -- scans the working tree, and only when non-empty also scans the movement's own base commit (git archive into a throwaway tempdir, reusing scan_repository() unmodified), blocking only findings absent from that baseline, matched on (path, rule, a content fingerprint of the flagged line) so line-number drift doesn't misclassify pre-existing debt as new; a denial names only the genuinely new finding(s). tests/test_nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py: 7 passed, including a regression reproducing the exact AC-1 live-bug findings (project/build_history.json, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003-local-relay-watch-command.json:155) against this repository's real state, proving both are now recognized as pre-existing. tests/test_orchestrator.py unaffected: 48 passed. tests/test_architecture_convergence.py: 22 passed. git diff --check clean. Repository privacy gate at PR time (main.py --repository-privacy-check, unmodified/out-of-scope full-tree scan): FAIL/5 pre-existing findings only. Live confirmation of the fix: this movement's own git push was denied once by 3 genuinely-new findings from untracked, gitignored data/logs/ runtime artifacts left over from local test runs (no git baseline possible for uncommitted files, a separate documented out-of-scope gap) -- removed as disposable local state, then the push succeeded cleanly through the fixed hook. Project-state updated (build_history.json, roadmap.json, CURRENT_STATE.md, docs/history/INDEX.md). PR #127 merged to main via 3efaa1ce per the standing relay#13 merge decision -- no separate merge RELAY_DECISION needed.
